more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Erythritol is a four-carbon sugar alcohol manufactured by carbohydrate fermentation and subsequent purification. It provides sweetness when added to the food or used in a table-top sweetener preparation. Produced by fermentation of carbohydrates with suitable food-grade yeasts. The erythritol is then purified and dried. The specified material is supplied as white crystalline material. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Produced by fermentation of carbohydrates with suitable food-grade yeasts. The erythritol is then purified and dried.
more_info.side_effects:
High food-use exposure estimates exceeded the limit.
Human studies establish dose-related diarrhoea; repeated diarrhoea may disturb fluid and electrolyte balance.
